outcome: Improve space, timetable, energy, maintenance, and service utilisation while protecting student and staff privacy.
overview: Campus timetables, occupancy, assets, work orders and energy are planned in separate systems, so rooms sit empty while other spaces overflow and maintenance stays reactive. This solution brings scheduling, facilities telemetry, service demand and aggregated occupancy signals into one governed operational layer, forecasts demand and recommends timetable, energy and maintenance actions. Occupancy is counted, never identified: no individual tracking, and planners approve every action before it reaches a building or work-order system. An eight-to-twelve-week baseline and one scheduling cycle test whether utilisation improves or controllable facilities cost falls in the pilot area, with savings normalised for weather and occupancy before any claim is made.

benefits.text: Improve teaching-space utilisation or reduce selected controllable facilities cost by a target 10% in the pilot area
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against a normalised campus baseline
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate on one pilot building or zone over a full scheduling cycle — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Cut timetable conflicts and overcrowding complaints by matching room allocation to forecast demand before publication
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on timetable-system integration depth and on how late course enrolment changes arrive

benefits.text: Move from reactive to condition-based maintenance on monitored assets, with every work order approved by a named planner
benefits.source: Reference design — anomaly detection raises a proposed work order; approval is a required human step
benefits.limits: Detection quality depends on sensor coverage and on the age and instrumentation of the estate

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); occupancy signals are aggregated at source and no identity-level location data is retained in the reference designs

notFor.situation: The institution wants identity-level tracking of students or staff around campus
notFor.why: The design counts occupancy in aggregate and rejects individual location tracking by policy — it is a privacy boundary, not a configuration option

notFor.situation: No digital timetable, asset register or metering data
notFor.why: Forecasting and optimisation need scheduled demand, asset identity and consumption baselines; without them recommendations cannot be grounded or verified

notFor.situation: The institution expects autonomous control of building plant during the proof of value
notFor.why: No unsafe automatic building action is permitted in the PoV; recommendations are advisory and approved by an operator before any control action

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns the estate, operational approval authority and the privacy and safety position · Duration: 8–12 weeks PoV; 16–28 weeks to scaled multi-campus deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, IoT and integration engineer, data scientist, controls specialist; customer facilities director, timetabling officer, sustainability lead, security and privacy reviewers · Support model: Business-hours support with out-of-hours cover for monitored critical assets; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor and controls-contractor escalation
1) Discovery, site survey and meter validation
2) Normalised baseline establishment
3) Integration and data-layer build
4) Forecasting and optimisation build with fail-safe design
5) Privacy, security and operational readiness review
6) Supervised PoV and verified savings review
deliverables: Forecast accuracy and optimisation thresholds met on the pilot area
Privacy review passed with aggregated occupancy only and no identity-level records
Every action planner-approved, with fail-safe limits and revert proven
Integration reconciliation between the platform, CMMS and BMS demonstrated
Operational UAT completed by facilities and timetabling teams
Savings normalised for weather and occupancy and confirmed by finance
effort: 8–12 weeks PoV; 16–28 weeks to scaled multi-campus deployment
